# A result series remembers geometry and time

[A frame number is not a simulation step, and neither one tells us the physical time. Store all three deliberately.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

This refactoring of `11_write_results` uses native `SnapshotSeries` in
place of the old example-only VTK wrapper. The field is deliberately
padded, the geometry is nontrivial, and the three saved states have
steps 0,4,8 at times 0,.25,.5:

$$
u(x,y,z,t)=1+x+2y+3z+t.
$$ {#eq-field}

These are prescribed fields for studying output. No PDE solver is hidden
inside this example.

## Register a field, then write output opportunities

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="series" dedent=4}
```

The VTK slot and raw binary slot borrow the same field. The series packs
only owned samples before writing, so halo storage does not leak into
either file. The field and its allocation must remain valid while the
series uses them. All communicator ranks participate in each write and
in `close`.

The frame ordinal chooses the filename suffix 0000,0001,0002. Simulation
steps and physical times are separate metadata. `close()` writes the
manifest and XDMF information and reports errors on the successful path;
relying only on destructor cleanup would lose that opportunity.

## Inspect the files before interpreting a picture

`results/lesson_manifest.json` records dimensions, spacing, origin,
field names, filename patterns, steps and times. VTK files include physical
geometry and an appended binary scalar array. The raw binary slot also
gets a generated XDMF time series, which supplies geometry and time to
the otherwise headerless arrays.

In serial, open `density_0000.vti` in a VTK-compatible viewer. In parallel,
the writer emits `.vti` pieces and a `.pvti` master with non-overlapping
point extents. Some VTK/ParaView readers do not assemble those pieces
into a single image; individual pieces remain readable. The generated
XDMF series describes the global binary field and is another route for
viewing the whole result.

## Verify the content, not just the existence of a file

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --source-root .. --launcher=none
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --source-root .. --ranks=2 --launcher=mpirun
```

The tests parse each VTK piece's XML and binary payload, reconstruct the
whole field, check origin and spacing, and compare each saved value with
@eq-field. They separately decode the binary frames and inspect the
manifest and XDMF times. None of the halo sentinel values should appear
in the saved fields.

Change the geometry in [the helper](../lesson.hpp), then check that the
header and physical sample values both change. Keep the [model](model.cpp)
and [input](input.json) with it. For actual simulation evolution, continue
with Cahn–Hilliard.
:::
